label: Flagellar motor
plain: The rotary motor at the foot of each flagellum. A rotor of rings sits in the inner membrane; stator units round it let protons into the cell and push on it; a straight drive shaft passes through the wall and the outer membrane to a flexible hook, which turns the long filament.

modelled.text: Cells has no model of this motor: no law of the engine drives it, and E. coli is proposed, not modelled. What is drawn is an illustration, built from sizes and counts that papers give.

frame.axis: out of the cell, along the flagellum
frame.zero: the middle of the inner membrane
frame.note: A position along the axis (`z_nm`) is how far a part's middle lies outside the middle of the inner membrane; a negative one lies in the cytoplasm. Across the axis every part is round it, unless it is a unit set round it at a radius.

n-diameters.text: Diameters of the LP ring complex, the S ring, the M ring, and the C ring are ~25 nm, ~24.5 nm, ~30 nm, and ~45 nm, respectively, in Salmonella.

n-ms.text: The MS ring is composed of the transmembrane protein FliF and is part of a rotor

n-cring.text: FliG, FliM, and FliN form the C ring on the cytoplasmic face of the MS ring.

n-cring-role.text: The C ring acts not only as a central part of the rotor for torque generation but also as a structural device to switch the direction of motor rotation in E. coli and Salmonella

n-lp.text: The L and P rings, which are formed by the lipoprotein FlgH and the periplasmic protein FlgI, respectively, are embedded in the outer membrane and the peptidoglycan (PG) layer, respectively, and they together act as a bearing for the rod.

n-stator-radius.text: The stator units are assembled on the FliG ring (Figure 1c), and so stator–rotor interactions occur about 20 nm away from the center of the C ring in Salmonella.

n-stators-10.text: The flagellar motor can accommodate about 10 stator units around a rotor in E. coli and Salmonella when the motor operates at high load

n-stators-dozen.text: A dozen MotAB complex are associated with the basal body to act as a stator unit in the motor but is gone during purification.
n-stators-dozen.where: the caption of the paper's Figure 1, headed "Salmonella flagellum"

n-stators-few.text: the stator number is decreased from 10 to a few when external load becomes quite low

n-motab.text: The MotAB complex is composed of four copies of MotA and two copies of MotB and acts as a transmembrane H+ channel

n-two-paths.text: The MotAB stator complex has two H+ pathways formed by MotA-TM3, MotA-TM4 and MotB-TM

n-pgb.text: The PGB domains of MotB (MotBPGB) and PomB (PomBPGB) bind to the PG layer to allow the MotAB and PomAB complexes to become an active stator unit around a rotor

n-inward.text: The flagellum of E. coli and Salmonella is a supramolecular rotary motor powered by an inward-directed H+ translocation through a transmembrane H+ channel of the MotAB stator complex and can spin in both CCW and CW directions without changing the direction of H+ flow.

n-ion-exterior.text: Asp-33 of Salmonella MotB, which corresponds to Asp-32 in E. coli MotB, is critical for the binding of H+ from the cell exterior

n-run-ccw.text: E. coli and Salmonella cells can swim in a straight line by bundling left-handed helical filaments behind the cell body (run) when all of them rotate in CCW direction.

n-tumble.text: When one or multiple motors switch the direction of rotation from CCW to CW, the flagellar bundle is disrupted, enabling the cell to tumble and change the swimming direction.

n-speed.text: The maximum motor speed reaches 300 revolutions per second in E. coli and Salmonella

n-gate.text: The type III protein export apparatus consists of an export gate complex made of five transmembrane proteins, FlhA, FlhB, FliP, FliQ and FliR, and a cytoplasmic ATPase ring complex consisting of FliH, FliI and FliJ

n-gate-place.text: The transmembrane export gate complex is located within the basal body MS ring and acts as a H+–protein antiporter to couple an inward-directed H+ translocation through the export gate with an outward-directed protein export

n-pqr.text: FliP, FliQ, and FliR form a right-handed helical assembly with a 5 FliP to 4 FliQ to 1 FliR stoichiometry inside the MS ring, and FliO is required for efficient assembly of the FliPQR complex

n-pqr-channel.text: The FliPQR complex has a central channel with a diameter of 1.5 nm

n-flha.text: FlhA forms a nonameric ring structure through its C-terminal cytoplasmic domain

n-atpase.text: FliH, FliI and FliJ form the cytoplasmic ATPase ring complex with a 12 FliH to 6 FliI to 1 FliJ stoichiometry

n-atpase-attach.text: The ATPase ring complex is associated with the basal body through interactions of FliH with FlhA and a C ring protein FliN

n-atpase-work.text: The FliI6 ring hydrolyzes ATP to activate the transmembrane export gate complex

n-rod.text: The rod is composed of three proximal rod proteins, FlgB, FlgC, FlgF, and the distal rod protein FlgG

n-flie.text: FliE is postulated to connect the MS ring and the most proximal part of the rod formed by FlgB

n-axial.text: The rod is straight and rigid against bending and twisting and acts as a drive shaft. The hook is supercoiled and flexible against bending and acts as a universal joint to smoothly transmit torque produced by the motor to the filament.

n-protofilaments.text: The axial structure of the bacterial flagellum is commonly a helical assembly composed of 11 protofilaments

n-hook-120.text: The Salmonella hook is formed by about 120 copies of the hook protein FlgE.

n-flik.text: The hook length is controlled by the molecular ruler protein FliK, which is secreted via a type III protein export apparatus during hook assembly

n-flic-30000.text: The flagellar filament of E. coli is formed by ~30,000 copies of flagellin, FliC.

n-flim-34.text: in spite of the switch complex contains ~34 FliM subunits, the binding of about 13 CheY-P molecules can reverse the motor

n-flim-flig.text: The middle domain of FliM (FliMM) binds to FliGM with a one-to-one stoichiometry to form the C ring wall

n-flin.text: FliMC and FliN together form a doughnut-shaped hetero-tetramer consisting of one copies of FliMC and three copies of FliN, and this hetero-tetrameric block produces a continuous spiral density along the circumference at the bottom edge of the C ring

n-chey.text: The binding of the phosphorylated form of CheY (CheY-P) to FliM and FliN induces the structural remodeling of the C ring responsible for the switching of direction of flagellar motor rotation from CCW to CW.

n-steps.text: The flagellar motor containing a single stator unit rotates with 26 steps per revolution in both CCW and CW directions

s-stators-11.text: The maximum number of stators, per flagellum, is at least 11
s-stators-11.where: the section "Bacteria – cost of the E. coli flagellum"

s-channels.text: each of which has two channels (Braun and Blair, 2001), and each channel passes 50 protons per revolution

s-copies.text: a single E. coli flagellum contains 1 FliJ protein (part of exporter), 10 FliD’s (filament cap), 100 FlgE’s (hook), and 104 FliCs (filament)
s-copies.note: "104" is 10⁴: the superscript is lost in the paper's text as saved.

s-380.text: The E. coli flagellum can spin at a maximal rate of 380 Hz

s-150.text: The mean swimming speed for Salmonella, a close relative of E. coli, occurs at a rotation rate of 150 Hz

z-filament-hook.text: This system consists of a long extracellular filament approximately 20 nm in diameter, a hook about 50 nm in length, and rotary bacterial flagellar motors (BFM) embedded in the cell envelope.

z-tube.text: The flagellar filament is a hollow tube 5–20 μm in length, with typical outer and inner diameters of 24 nm and 2 nm, respectively

z-cring.text: Cryo-electron microscopy has revealed that the C-ring diameters are 416 Å for CCW and 407 Å for CW, indicating that the C-ring subunits are closer together in the CW state

z-chez.text: CheZ catalyzes the dephosphorylation of CheY-P, terminating the signal and resetting the chemotaxis system to prepare for the next round of signal transduction

d-ccw-view.text: its filaments are gathered in a helical bundle behind the cell body, which rotates in a counter-clockwise (CCW) fashion when viewed from behind the cell

d-cw-distal.text: it remains in semi-coiled form during a time ts rotating in the CW direction (when viewed from the distal end)

d-40.text: The helical filament of a flagellum, typically O(5–10) μm in length and 40 nm in diameter

d-rate.text: at a rate of about 100–200 Hz

m-im-om.text: As shown in Figure 1E, the averaged distance from the IM to the OM were somewhat greater in the Lpp+21 strain (32–36 nm) compared to the isogenic wild-type strain (30–32 nm)

m-of.text: To establish the extent to which the periplasm had been remodeled in the Lpp+21 strain of E. coli, we compared the periplasms of WT and Lpp+21 strains using electron cryotomography

m-hyper.text: the average distance from the middle of the IM density to the middle of the OM density was increased in both strains under hyperosmotic conditions when compared to previously reported data where cells were grown in standard laboratory media

m-om-pg.text: In wild-type E. coli (i.e. Lpp+ OmpA), the centre-centre distance in the simulations is 10.7±2.2 nm (Figure 4B), similar to the 9.7–10.8 nm measured in intact cells

m-om-pg-how.text: We also compared our simulations to the distances that were measured by EM (centre of the OM to centre of the PG).

u-names.text: The recommended names of the entries, as data/proteins/ecoli/proteins.tsv holds them (column `name`): P33235 "Flagellar hook-associated protein 1", P29744 "Flagellar hook-associated protein 3", P76010 "Flagellar brake protein YcgR", P0ABX8 "Flagellar protein FliL", P76297 "Flagellar protein FlhE", Q47154 "Putative truncated flagellar export/assembly protein LafU".

s-load.text: in E. coli rotation rates decrease with an increased load

m-swim.text: To obtain clear images of the flagella as they rotated at angular frequencies ∼100 Hz, it was necessary to take short exposures

k-flif.text: Here, using cryoEM structural analysis of the flagellar basal body and the MS ring formed by full-length FliF from Salmonella enterica, we show that the native MS ring is formed by 34 FliF subunits with no symmetry variation.

k-sring.text: The S ring is made up of 34 RBM3 domains horizontally packed with their major axis oriented in the radial direction to form a ring with a diameter of 24 nm.

nakamura2019.text: Nakamura S, Minamino T (2019) Flagella-Driven Motility of Bacteria. Biomolecules 9:279.

schavemaker2022.text: Schavemaker PE, Lynch M (2022) Flagellar energy costs across the tree of life. eLife 11:e77266.

dvoriashyna2021.text: Dvoriashyna M, Lauga E (2021) Hydrodynamics and direction change of tumbling bacteria. PloS one 16:e0254551.

kawamoto2021.text: Kawamoto A, Miyata T, Makino F, Kinoshita M, Minamino T, Imada K, Kato T, Namba K (2021) Native flagellar MS ring is formed by 34 subunits with 23-fold and 11-fold subsymmetries. Nature Communications 12:4223.

pdb.reading: Copies are those each entry's own record states; widths and heights are the motor agent's own reading of the coordinates (alpha carbons only), not checked against the papers that describe the entries.

decided: The user, 16 November 2026: the motor turns, at real-life speed, as part of the Cell view's flux, and slowed only when flux is slowed; "Look closer" from the foot's panel; protons wait; the Protein Data Bank may be used. The parts are drawn from the papers here; no shape is taken from a structure; some counts and sizes are, each with its entry and the organism its record states (the coordinator's ruling of the same day).
